headlines: MIAMI-DADE APPROVES $1.02 MILLION INCENTIVE FOR MIAMI VICE MOVIE
NEW MIAMI VICE FILM BRINGS JOBS AND SPENDING HOME
MIAMI VICE RETURNS WITH MILLIONS PROMISED FOR LOCAL WORKERS
posts.article:
Miami-Dade County commissioners approved a $1.02 million production incentive package Tuesday to help fund the upcoming film Miami Vice '85. The movie will star Austin Butler as Sonny Crockett and Michael B. Jordan as Ricardo Tubbs, directed by Joseph Kosinski.

To secure the single reimbursement payment, filmmakers must invest heavily in the community. Requirements include spending at least $10 million in Miami-Dade County, hiring county residents for 30 percent or more of the below-the-line local crew, and setting up county production offices.

Additionally, the team must use local studios and allocate at least half of vendor spending, or $5 million, to area businesses. The movie hits theaters in May 2028.

headlines: COUNTY ADVANCES $100 MILLION PLAN TO REDEVELOP SHUTTERED SEAQUARIUM
NEW MARINA PROPOSED FOR MIAMI SEAQUARIUM
WHAT WILL HAPPEN TO OUR ICONIC MIAMI SEAQUARIUM SITE
posts.article:
Miami-Dade commissioners voted unanimously on Tuesday to advance a 100 million dollar redevelopment proposal for the shuttered Seaquarium site. The county-owned, 38-acre waterfront property closed down last year following an eviction battle centered on animal-welfare concerns.

Developer David Martin of Terra plans to lease the land for 99 years, keeping the Seaquarium name while building an aquarium, public baywalk, restaurants, event venues, a 325-slip marina, and drydock storage for over 500 boats.

Environmental advocates urged officials to delay the action. Rachel Silverstein of Miami Waterkeeper raised alarms over water quality, coral, and seagrass damage. Martin stated his design reduces environmental impact on Biscayne Bay. A final commission vote is expected by the end of the year.
